histories.MatterHistoryActionText: The President called for nominations for the two at-large vacancies on this Commission, which were submitted as follows: Council Member Evans nominated Payton Robbins and Mary Nell Bryan; Council Member Hill nominated Jordan Parentau; Council Member Horton nominated Heather Derrick; Council Member Johnston nominated Penny Adams; Council Member Suara nominated Dr. Yasin Kokoye; Council Member Vo nominated Jaing Jing; Council Member Cortese nominated Michelle Spazziano; Council Member Bradford nominated Jessica Schultz; Council Member Hancock nominated Dr. Kelly Boyd and Donna Mobley; Council Member Styles and Ellis nominated Annette Filippone; Council Member Weiner nominated Carolyn Bennick Brown. The President called for nominations for the one vacancy to be filled by a representative from a local nonprofit organization dedicated to animal welfare, which were submitted as follows: Council Member Taylor nominated Lisa Steddar; Council Member Styles nominated Brandon Dyce; Council Member Weiner nominate Becky Carter. The President called for nominations for a non-voting Council Member to serve on this Commission, which were submitted as follows: Council Member Styles nominated Council Member Evans; Council Member Weiner nominated Council Member Bradford; Council Member Evans withdrew her nomination. The President declared the nominations closed, with an election to be conducted at the September 1, 2026 Council meeting.

histories.MatterHistoryActionText: The Rules, Confirmations, and Public Elections Committee recommended the nominees. The President called for an election to fill two at-large vacancies on the Metro Animal Care and Control Commission. Nominations previously made were Payton Robbins, Jourdan Parenteau, Penny Adams, Jing Geng, Michelle Spaziano, Jessica Schultz, Dr. Kelli Boyd, and Donna Mobley. The following vote was taken on the nominated candidates: Jordan Parenteau (18): Suara, Allen, Hill, Toombs, Cortese, Capp, Huffman, Gregg, Vo, Druffel, Preptit, Nash, Ellis, Rutherford, Styles, Lee, Ewing, and Spain; Jing Geng (16): Suara, Porterfield, Evans-Segall, Allen, Kimbrough, Toombs, Gamble, Parker, Harrell, Vo, Cash, Preptit, Ellis, Sepulveda, Styles, and Lee; Dr. Kelli Boyd (11): Hill, Kimbrough, Cortese, Hancock, Webb, Bradford, Druffel, Johnston, Nash, Benton, and Ewing; Jessica Schultz (9): Evans-Segall, Parker, Capp, Benedict, Eslick, Evans, Bradford, Huffman, and Sepulveda; Payton Robbins (9): Benedict, Harrell, Webb, Eslick, Evans, Gregg, Benton, Rutherford, and Spain; Penny Adams (2): Cash, Johnston; Donna Mobley (1): Hancock; Michelle Spaziano (0); Abstain (0). The president declared that Jourdan Parenteau was elected to the Commission, and that another round of voting would be conducted to fill the remaining vacancy. The following vote was taken in the second round of voting: Jing Geng (18): Suara, Porterfield, Evans-Segall, Allen, Kimbrough, Toombs, Gamble, Parker, Capp, Harrell, Gregg, Vo, Cash, Preptit, Ellis, Sepulveda, Styles, and Lee; Dr. Kelli Boyd (10): Hill, Cortese, Hancock, Webb, Eslick, Druffel, Johnston, Nash, Benton, and Ewing; Payton Robbins (4): Benedict, Evans, Rutherford, and Spain; Jessica Schultz (2): Bradford and Huffman; Penny Adams (0); Donna Mobley (0); Michelle Spaziano (0); Abstain (0). The president declared that Jing Geng was elected to the Commission.
